facts.fact: The AMC-MAD congress report on Datasanté's site states that, at the cyber-health round table of 5 November 2024 attended by the health ministry (DGFS) and DEPSI, the electronic personal medical record was described as functional in some private establishments and some basic health centres (CSB), with technical and financial obstacles slowing implementation at scale; no figures are given.
The AMC-MAD congress report says the electronic medical record works in 'certain' private establishments and CSB as at the round table of 5 November 2024 and gives no count or share of facilities.

The congress report states that the computerised patient record software used in Madagascar's community medical centres is Datasanté's, that the Datasanté team trained practitioners on it and on the DATABOX on 7 November 2024, and that AMC-MAD (the community doctors' association) and Datasanté signed a convention on 6 November 2024 continuing their partnership and extending the network of front-line doctors using it.

The congress report states that the convention signed on 6 November 2024 between AMC-MAD and Datasanté provides for Datasanté's continued logistical and financial support; no state funding of the patient record software is mentioned, and the round table called for more support from the ministry.

systems.country_label: dossier patient informatisé Datasanté; logiciel LOGDS, which takes over from DSMG; DATABOX
systems.owner: Datasanté (French association) with AMC-MAD, the Association des Médecins Communautaires de Madagascar
systems.tiers: community medical centres (private community doctors' practices); computerisation began in 2012 with 5 beta testers
functional in some private establishments and some CSB

note: The round table's statement about the electronic record is general and is not tied by the text to Datasanté alone, so it is recorded under its own label. Events of November 2024 fall outside the twelve-month window, so no last12 fact.
